title: Anymake board-state.json
description: The structured spine of the Anymake agile board. Agents append events to events[]; the orchestrator is the sole writer of the snapshot (stories[], in_flight, concurrency, updated). The hub (main agent) writes the optional `session` object once at session start and appends session-lifecycle events to session-log.jsonl (NOT to events[]) — see ADR-013. BOARD.md is a rendered projection of this file. The kanban UI reads it directly. One source of truth (INV-004). Validate any instance with `node .opencode/validate-board-state.mjs <path>` (or `npm run validate-board`); AGENTS/orchestrator.md and skills/anymake-dispatch/SKILL.md require that run after every write.

updated.description: ISO-8601 timestamp of the last orchestrator reconciliation

max.description: Maximum concurrent in-flight stories. max=1 reproduces the older sequential behavior exactly. Bounded at 10: beyond that, host Agent/Task contention and merge-conflict rate dominate, and the orchestrator's stall detection stops being able to tell a slow story from a stuck one. Raise the ceiling here deliberately, with a note saying why — do not treat the bound as advisory.

current.description: Current count of in-flight stories (maintained by the orchestrator)

in_flight.description: Story IDs currently in progress (maintained by the orchestrator)

session.description: Current session context. Written by the hub skill (the main agent) ONCE at session start (single read-modify-write) and updated in place on phase/step advance. The orchestrator does not touch this object. Absent during pure build-loop runs that don't surface a session (backward compatible). See ADR-013.

id.description: Session identifier (e.g. ISO timestamp + short random suffix)

planner.description: Planner re-dispatches. Arbiter: one re-dispatch for an incomplete brief, then escalate.

worker.description: Worker re-dispatches. Arbiter: 2 for failure_type=environment; 0 for implementation (immediate escalation). 2 is the loosest applicable ceiling.

validation.description: Validation FAIL retries. Arbiter: 1 (straight back to the Worker, no Planner re-run), then escalate on the 2nd FAIL.

experience.description: Experience Runner retries. Arbiter: 1 for a FAIL verdict; 2 for an ESCALATE(environment-failure) re-dispatch of the runner itself. 2 is the loosest applicable ceiling.

retries.description: Per-stage retry counters. The maximum on each field is the loosest ceiling that can apply to that stage under AGENTS/arbiter.md's Retry Policy Matrix. The POLICY, not the schema, decides which ceiling applies to which failure kind — e.g. a worker environment failure allows 2 re-dispatches while an implementation failure allows 0, and both increment the same 'worker' counter. A value within bounds is therefore necessary but not sufficient for policy compliance; a value over bounds is always a bug.

touches_files.description: File paths the story's technical tasks will modify (emitted by the Planner in the task brief, used for parallel-dispatch conflict detection: two stories conflict iff their touches_files sets intersect). REQUIRED — an empty array is the explicit statement 'this story declares no file conflicts', which is a fact the orchestrator can act on. An absent field is not: it is indistinguishable from a Planner that never computed it, and silently reads as 'conflicts with nothing'.

events.description: Append-only event log. Agents append; the orchestrator reconciles the snapshot from this log. Lost appends are acceptable — the dispatch log line in BOARD.md's Run Log is the durable belt-and-suspenders record.

story.description: Story ID this event pertains to (null for session-lifecycle events — see ADR-013)

agent.description: Agent that emitted the event (worker, validator, experience-runner, orchestrator, planner, dispatch, hub)

session.description: Session ID the event belongs to (present for session-lifecycle events, absent for build-loop events)

artifact.description: File path of the artifact produced (for artifact-type events)
